subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equations of the straight lines passing through the point of intersection of the lines 3x + 2y + 4 = 0 and 2x + 5y = 1 whose distance from (2, −1) is 2.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.155, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 10. **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split puts two marks on each of the two pieces of real work — finding the meeting point and turning the distance condition into an equation in m — two more on solving it, and one each on writing the line through the point and on reporting both answers. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Both answers were substituted back before they were written: y − 1 = 0 passes through (−2, 1) and its distance from (2, −1) is |−1 − 1| = 2, and 4x + 3y + 5 = 0 gives −8 + 3 + 5 = 0 at (−2, 1) and |8 − 3 + 5|/5 = 2 at (2, −1). The pair was also reached a second way, through the family (3x + 2y + 4) + λ(2x + 5y − 1) = 0, which gives λ = 1/14 and λ = −3/2 and the same two lines.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the point every answer must pass through, and say why the question has two answers.

steps.label: Find the point of intersection
steps.margin_note: The first two marks. Make one column of coefficients match, subtract, and put the value back into either line for the second coordinate.

recall.must_convey: That the two given lines meet at P(−2, 1).

steps.why: Every line asked for has to pass through this one point, so nothing else in the question can be started until it is found.
common_mistakes: Writing 2x + 5y = 1 as 2x + 5y + 1 = 0 when moving the 1 across.
Solving the pair but forgetting to put the value back to find y.
steps.memory_tip: Match one column, subtract, then put the value BACK. Move the 1 across as −1, not +1.

steps.label: Write the line through it
steps.margin_note: One mark. Test the vertical line first, then write the point-slope form through P and bring it to ax + by + c = 0 shape.

so the required line has a slope m.

recall.must_convey: That the line through P is y − 1 = m(x + 2), after the vertical line is ruled out.

steps.why: The slope form misses vertical lines, so the vertical line through P is tested separately and ruled out before m is introduced.
common_mistakes: Starting from y = mx + c and never using the point P.
Never checking the vertical line, so a possible answer is not ruled out.
steps.memory_tip: The slope form cannot describe a vertical line, so check x = −2 by hand first, then use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

steps.label: Apply the distance condition
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Put (2, −1) into |ax + by + c|/√(a² + b²) for the line just written, set it equal to 2, and take the common factor 2 out.

recall.must_convey: That putting (2, −1) into the distance formula gives |2m + 1| = √(m² + 1).
accept: put two comma minus one into the distance formula
mod four m plus two over root m squared plus one equals two

distance formula lo two comma minus one pettali

steps.why: The distance condition is the only equation in the question, and writing it with the modulus kept is what turns a geometry statement into algebra.
common_mistakes: Putting the coordinates of P into the distance formula instead of (2, −1).
Cancelling the 2 on the right without dividing the left side as well.
steps.memory_tip: The POINT goes into the formula, the LINE gives the coefficients. Here 4m + 2 has a factor 2 that cancels the 2 on the right.

steps.label: Solve for the slope
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Square, cancel the 1 on both sides, and take m out as a common factor. Never divide by m — that throws away the answer m = 0.

recall.must_convey: That squaring gives 3m² + 4m = 0, so m = 0 or m = −4/3.
accept: square both sides and get three m squared plus four m equals zero
take m as a common factor to get m equals zero or minus four by three
the two slopes are zero and minus four over three

do not divide by m

steps.why: Squaring removes the modulus and both roots are kept, because the two lines through P at distance 2 are genuinely two different lines.
common_mistakes: Dividing by m and losing the root m = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Take m OUT as a factor, never divide by it. Dividing by m loses the line y = 1.

steps.label: Write both lines
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Put each slope back into y − 1 = m(x + 2) and clear the fractions. Both lines are part of the answer.

recall.must_convey: That the two lines are y − 1 = 0 and 4x + 3y + 5 = 0.

steps.why: The question asks for equations, in the plural, so both slopes have to be carried back through the point-slope form and written out.
common_mistakes: Reporting only one of the two lines.
Leaving the answer as a slope instead of an equation.
steps.memory_tip: Two slopes means TWO equations. Put each one back into the point-slope form and clear the fraction.
